# Doefin brand: overview

How Doefin looks and how it writes, on the website, in the app, on X and LinkedIn, in email and in decks. The writing matters most. If you read one file, read `voice.md`. If you write anything long, read `matteo/thinking.md` too.

## Doefin in one line

**Trade and hedge Bitcoin hashrate exposure through markets on mining difficulty.**

When there is room for more, in Matteo's words: Doefin provides markets for trading and hedging Bitcoin hashrate exposure. Our contracts reference future Bitcoin mining difficulty. We help miners assess that exposure and give professional investors a way to trade their views through defined market outcomes.

How a market works, in one sentence: each market asks whether difficulty will be at or above a set level at a specified Bitcoin block, and positions are funded and settled in cbBTC.

Hashrate is what people are exposed to; difficulty decides the contract. Do not call Doefin "hashrate derivatives" or a "prediction market".

Company line for footers, documents and decks: Doefin, Port Louis, Mauritius.

## Who we write for

Miners and the people who finance them, and funds and trading desks. All of them are professional investors. They know mining and check the maths. They stop reading at the first line of hype. We never write for retail readers.

Miners hedge; investors and desks trade a view. Name each reader and what it does, rather than writing for everyone at once.

## The short version

- `ink` and white do most of the work. Doefin Blue marks the one thing to look at.
- Flat colour. No gradients, glows or frosted glass.
- Manrope for everything, with figures that line up in columns.
- Numbers come with their unit, and with a date and a source whenever they can change.
- Short sentences, real numbers and the qualifiers that make them true. Write it the way Matteo would explain it to a miner.
- No contractions.
- Use the logo files as they are. Never redraw, stretch or recolour them.

## Before anything goes out

- Does the first line get straight to the subject?
- Is every number exact, with its unit, its date and its qualifier?
- If it says what Doefin lets people do, does it say what can go wrong, next to the claim?
- Did it pass the copy checker (`tools/check_copy.py`)?
- Is it free of promises, real returns and anything aimed at retail?
- Does it contain one of the five kinds Matteo reviews first (`compliance.md`)? Then send it to him.
